questions.skill: Solve simple systems by inspection
questions.prompt: Without solving, explain why this system has no solution. 3x + 2y = 5 3x + 2y = 6
questions.prompt_markup:
Without solving, explain why this system has no solution.
3x + 2y = 5
3x + 2y = 6
questions.correct_answer: The same expression, 3x + 2y, cannot equal both 5 and 6.

questions.skill: Solve simple systems by inspection
questions.prompt: Without solving, how many solutions does this system have? Explain. y = 4x - 1 y = 4x + 3
questions.prompt_markup:
Without solving, how many solutions does this system have? Explain.
y = 4x - 1
y = 4x + 3
questions.correct_answer: None. The lines have the same slope and different y-intercepts, so they are parallel.

questions.skill: Solve simple systems by inspection

questions.correct_answer: One. The slopes are different, so the lines cross once (at (0, 5)).

questions.skill: Recognize equivalent expressions
questions.prompt: Is 2x + 2y equivalent to 2(x + y)? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup: Is 2x + 2y equivalent to 2(x + y)? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. By the distributive property, 2(x + y) = 2x + 2y.

questions.domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
questions.skill: Classify lines as parallel, perpendicular, or neither from their equations
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Are the lines y = 2x + 1 and 4x - 2y = 6 parallel, perpendicular, or neither? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup: Are the lines y = 2x + 1 and 4x - 2y = 6 parallel, perpendicular, or neither? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Parallel; both have slope 2 (and different y-intercepts).

questions.prompt_markup: Are the lines 3x + y = 2 and x - 3y = 9 parallel, perpendicular, or neither? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Perpendicular; the slopes are -3 and 1/3, and their product is -1.
